subject: physiology
title: Islet Microanatomy, Beta Cells, and Insulin Exocytosis

steps.tx: The endocrine pancreas consists of one to two million microscopic micro-organs known as the **islets of Langerhans**, scattered throughout exocrine acinar tissue. Islets contain four major hormone-secreting cell types: insulin-secreting beta cells (sixty percent), glucagon-secreting alpha cells (twenty-five percent), somatostatin-secreting delta cells (ten percent), and pancreatic polypeptide cells.
steps.say: Islets of Langerhans contain sixty percent beta cells making insulin, twenty-five percent alpha cells making glucagon, and delta cells.

rows: Anabolic storage of glucose, lipids, protein
Paracrine inhibition of both insulin and glucagon
Inhibits gallbladder contraction and pancreatic secretion

steps.tx: Microvascular blood flow within the islet proceeds from the center outward in a centrifugal direction. Consequently, arterial blood flows past centrally located beta cells before bathing peripheral alpha and delta cells, allowing high local concentrations of **secreted insulin** to directly inhibit adjacent alpha cells and suppress glucagon output.
steps.say: Centrifugal blood flow carries high concentrations of insulin from the central beta core outward to suppress alpha cells.

left.title: Centrifugal Microcirculation
points: Central afferent arteriole penetrates islet core
Blood perfuses central beta cells first
Flows radially outward to peripheral alpha and delta mantle
Insulin directly suppresses glucagon gene transcription

right.title: Paracrine Cross-Regulation
points: Delta cell somatostatin potently inhibits both insulin and glucagon
Alpha cell glucagon stimulates insulin secretion directly
Beta cell amylin co-secreted with insulin inhibits glucagon
Disrupted in type 1 diabetes, producing paradoxical hyperglucagonemia

steps.tx: Beta cells couple ambient extracellular glucose concentrations to insulin secretion through an elegant stimulus-secretion mechanism. Extracellular glucose enters beta cells via the bidirectional, non-saturable facilitated glucose transporter **GLUT2**, which possesses a high Km of fifteen to twenty millimoles per litre.
steps.say: Glucose enters beta cells through GLUT2, which has a high Km that allows it to match intracellular levels to blood sugar.

nodes.label: Postprandial Hyperglycaemia Drives Glucose into Beta Cell via Apical GLUT2
Glucokinase Phosphorylates Glucose to Glucose-6-Phosphate (Rate-Limiting Sensor)
Mitochondrial Glycolysis and Krebs Cycle Elevate Intracellular ATP/ADP Ratio
ATP Closes Inward-Rectifying K-ATP Channels, Eliciting Membrane Depolarization

steps.tx: Inside the beta cell, glucose is immediately phosphorylated to glucose-six-phosphate by the monomeric enzyme **glucokinase**, functioning as the true glucose sensor of the beta cell. Because glucokinase has a low affinity and lacks product inhibition, the rate of glucose phosphorylation parallels extracellular glycaemia across physiological ranges.
steps.say: Glucokinase acts as the beta cell glucose sensor, setting the rate of glycolysis in proportion to blood sugar levels.

left.title: Pancreatic Glucokinase (Hexokinase IV)
points: High Km (~8 to 10 mM); low affinity matching postprandial glucose
Not inhibited by its reaction product (glucose-6-phosphate)
Phosphorylation rate varies linearly with circulating glycaemia
Mutations cause maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY-2)

right.title: Hexokinase I-III (Peripheral Tissues)
points: Very low Km (< 0.1 mM); extremely high affinity
Fully saturated even at profound hypoglycaemic levels
Potently inhibited by glucose-6-phosphate product feedback
Ensures constant basal glucose utilization in brain and muscle

steps.tx: Accelerated intracellular glycolysis and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation generate abundant adenosine triphosphate, markedly increasing the cytosolic ATP-to-ADP ratio. This metabolic shift directly closes **ATP-sensitive potassium channels**, preventing further potassium efflux and depolarizing the beta-cell plasma membrane from minus seventy millivolts to minus forty millivolts.
steps.say: Rising ATP closes potassium channels, depolarizing the beta cell membrane to open voltage-gated calcium channels.

nodes.label: Elevated ATP Binds Kir6.2 Subunit, Closing K-ATP Channels
Arrests K+ Efflux; Membrane Depolarizes from -70 mV to -40 mV
Voltage-Gated L-Type Calcium Channels Open -> Influx of Extracellular Ca2+
SNARE-Mediated Exocytosis of Pre-Formed Insulin Storage Granules

steps.tx: Membrane depolarization triggers the opening of voltage-gated L-type calcium channels, producing a dramatic surge in intracellular calcium. Calcium activates synaptotagmin and SNARE core complexes, eliciting explosive exocytosis of dense-core secretory granules containing **mature human insulin** and stoichiometric quantities of connecting peptide.
steps.say: Calcium influx triggers SNARE proteins to fuse insulin granules with the membrane, releasing insulin and C-peptide.

vis.alt: Insulin granule exocytosis and beta cell microarchitecture
vis.caption: Islet beta cell stimulus-secretion coupling, calcium-mediated exocytosis, and proinsulin processing.

steps.tx: Oral sulfonylurea medications like glimepiride and gliclazide bind the sulfonylurea receptor one subunit of the **K-ATP channel complex**. By pharmacologically closing these channels independently of ambient glucose, sulfonylureas trigger continuous membrane depolarization and insulin exocytosis, explaining their characteristic risk of iatrogenic hypoglycemia.
steps.say: Sulfonylureas chemically close K-ATP channels, stimulating insulin secretion independently of ambient glucose levels.

vis.alt: Sulfonylurea pharmacology and beta cell channel targets
vis.caption: SUR1 receptor binding, K-ATP channel blockade, and pharmacotherapeutic insulin secretagogues.

steps.tx: During proinsulin processing in the Golgi apparatus, endopeptidases cleave connecting peptide, yielding active insulin and equimolar **connecting C-peptide**. Because hepatic extraction clears fifty percent of newly secreted insulin on first pass while C-peptide escapes hepatic degradation, serum C-peptide serves as the gold-standard biomarker of endogenous beta-cell reserve.
steps.say: C-peptide is co-secreted with insulin in equal amounts, serving as an accurate blood marker of natural insulin production.

rows: Reflects acute biologically active systemic levels
Accurate measure of endogenous beta-cell secretory reserve
